## Choice of library

The same pipeline is applied to leaf area index (LAI), which rises and then falls during the season, by changing `var = "lai"`. Least squares is used for all libraries here.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
trl <- make_trajectories(traj, drv, var = "lai")
P_poly <- cached("cv_lai_poly.rds", cross_validate(Theta, trl, fit_ols))
```
:::


As an alternative library, a B-spline basis in thermal time with the other three drivers entering linearly:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
B <- bs(as.vector(drv$U[, , "TT"]), df = 6)
others <- matrix(drv$U[, , -1], ncol = 3, dimnames = list(NULL, c("DL", "RAW", "RAD")))
Theta_spl <- array(cbind(B, others), c(dim(drv$U)[1:2], 9),
                   dimnames = list(NULL, NULL, c(paste0("B", 1:6), colnames(others))))
P_spl <- cached("cv_lai_spline.rds", cross_validate(Theta_spl, trl, fit_ols))

base <- lookup_trajectory(trl)
round(rbind(`cubic polynomial` = evaluate(P_poly, trl),
            `B-spline in TT` = evaluate(P_spl, trl),
            baseline = evaluate(base, trl)), 3)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
                 trajectory_rmse fixed_day_rmse maturity_rmse
cubic polynomial           0.925          1.272         1.039
B-spline in TT             0.532          0.664         0.562
baseline                   0.473          0.687         0.637
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
models <- c("cubic polynomial", "B-spline in TT", "baseline")
days <- 2:dim(trl$Y)[3] + trl$das0 - 1
rmse <- function(P, model) {
  data.frame(das = days, rmse = rmse_by_day(P, trl), model = model)
}
d <- rbind(rmse(P_poly, models[1]), rmse(P_spl, models[2]),
           rmse(base, models[3]))
d$model <- factor(d$model, models)

ggplot(d[d$das <= 155, ], aes(das, rmse, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "blue", "grey") +
  labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "held-out LAI RMSE") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  legend_top()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](08-limitations_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=1036.8}
:::
:::


A cubic polynomial in the standardised drivers cannot represent the rise and fall of LAI, and its error is larger than that of the baseline throughout. The spline library is considerably better. When the model is inaccurate, the library should be examined before the fitting method.

## Collinear drivers

Thermal time and day length have a correlation of 0.97. Fitting the same model to the odd and to the even seasons of one genotype gives different coefficients but similar growth rates.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
d <- make_design(Theta, tr, "g114")
odd <- fit_ols(d$X[d$season %% 2 == 1, ], d$dy[d$season %% 2 == 1])
even <- fit_ols(d$X[d$season %% 2 == 0, ], d$dy[d$season %% 2 == 0])
round(rbind(odd, even)[, c("TT", "TT^2", "DL", "DL^2")], 3)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
         TT   TT^2    DL   DL^2
odd  -0.067 -0.037 0.039 -0.065
even -0.025 -0.033 0.006 -0.055
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
rate <- cbind(1, d$X) %*% cbind(odd, even)      # growth rate on all days
c(correlation = cor(rate[, 1], rate[, 2]),
  max_difference = max(abs(rate[, 1] - rate[, 2])))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   correlation max_difference 
    0.98748717     0.03865562 
```


:::
:::


The data determine the combined effect of correlated drivers better than each coefficient, so response curves are preferable to individual coefficients for interpretation.

## Accumulation of error

The regression is performed on daily increments, whereas the prediction is their cumulative sum. A small bias in the daily increment therefore accumulates.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
P <- cached("cv_stlsq.rds", cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq))
step_error <- P[, , -1] - P[, , -dim(P)[3]]           # predicted increments
step_error <- step_error - (tr$Y[, , -1] - tr$Y[, , -dim(tr$Y)[3]])
c(daily_increment_rmse = sqrt(mean(step_error^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
  trajectory_rmse = evaluate(P, tr)[[1]])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
daily_increment_rmse      trajectory_rmse 
          0.02794568           0.52631617 
```


:::
:::


For this reason the model is assessed on the simulated trajectory and not on the daily increments.
